group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-10-03 (tool=LEGEND-research): 'Chang NS[au]' 138, 'Chang NS[au] AND WWOX' 66, 'Hsu LJ[au]' 103, 'Hsu LJ[au] AND WWOX' 30.
group_assessment.weighting: Five of the six papers in this group come from one laboratory lineage (Chang N-S / Hsu L-J, National Cheng Kung University). That laboratory originated WWOX and carries the gene's largest single output, so its measurements carry full weight; what it does NOT carry is independence. Two of its subjects are exclusive to it: 'Zfra NOT Chang NS[au]' returns 1 record and that record is an unrelated zebrafish androgen-receptor paper matching the string by accident; 'TIAF1 NOT Chang NS[au]' returns 5 of 20. The autophagy axis is the opposite case and is the reason this group is readable as a contradiction at all: 'WWOX AND autophagy' returns 10 records and 8 of them are from neither Chang NS nor Hsu LJ.
group_assessment.note: Research-group knowledge base is excluded from the public edition; this rests on measured PubMed counts and on the papers' own author lists.

corpus_crossquery.query: What does the corpus already assert about this paper, and does any of it misreport the direction of effect?
corpus_crossquery.finding: CORPUS-STUB-147, LIT-0165 and LIT-EX-005 all claim PMID 41677633 - two literature records for one identity, which registry_records.py itself flags AMBIGUOUS - and DL-MECH-016 carries the lysosomal statement. None of the four records the direction that decides transfer: in this paper WWOX LOSS is protective under serum starvation (higher viability, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, lower ROS in Wwox-null MEFs). The registry title also drops the final 's' of 'Stress Responses'.

entries.proposition: UNDER SERUM STARVATION THE WWOX-NULL CELL IS THE SURVIVING CELL. This is the direction that transfers, and it is the opposite of the protective reading of WWOX: loss of the gene preserves viability under this stress.
entries.snippet: Wwox+/+ MEFs showed a significantly enhanced reduction in cell viability as compared with Wwox−/− MEFs after serum starvation for 72 h

entries.proposition: THE MITOCHONDRIAL ENDPOINT MOVES WITH THE SAME SIGN: WWOX PRESENCE IS WHAT COLLAPSES THE MEMBRANE POTENTIAL. Mitochondrial membrane potential is a candidate rescue readout, and in this system it is WWOX-dependent.
entries.snippet: we detected a significant reduction in MMP in Wwox+/+ MEFs after serum starvation in a time-dependent manner

entries.proposition: THE LYSOSOMAL ROUTE RESTS ON PHARMACOLOGICAL INHIBITORS AND STATIC WESTERNS, NOT ON A FLUX ASSAY. No autophagic-flux measurement (LC3-II turnover, p62) is made anywhere in this paper; the route is inferred from which inhibitor rescues which band.
entries.snippet: The presence of E64d and pepstatin A reversed Bcl-XL and Mcl-1 protein downregulation after serum starvation in Wwox+/+ MEFs

experimental_context.treatment: serum starvation 32 h, E64d 30 uM or pepstatin A 15 uM in the last 4-8 h

entries.proposition: ONE OF THE TWO LYSOSOME-ALKALINISING AGENTS DOES NOT RESCUE, AND THE RUNNING TEXT NAMES ONLY THE ONE THAT DOES. In Figure S3B the Mcl-1 loss is rescued by chloroquine (0.37 starved to 0.90 and 0.88) and NOT by ammonium chloride (0.31 and 0.30, i.e. no rescue), while the Results sentence reports chloroquine alone. Incomplete is not false, and a reader taking the sentence alone will over-read the lysosomal attribution.

entries.proposition: WWOX DOES NOT BIND THE CARGO. The mechanism is left open by the authors themselves; nothing here licenses a direct WWOX-Bcl-XL or WWOX-Mcl-1 interaction.
entries.snippet: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed that neither Bcl-XL nor Mcl-1 physically interacted with WWOX.

entries.proposition: THE AUTHORS THEMSELVES NAME THE MISSING CONTROL: no genetic test of the lysosomal/autophagic route was done, so the pathway attribution rests on drugs with known pleiotropy.
entries.snippet: Because pharmacological inhibitors may have pleiotropic effects, knockdown of essential genes involved in the autophagy or lysosomal degradation pathway using RNA interference tools needs to be tested for verification.

entries.proposition: ROS IS NOT DIFFERENT AT BASELINE; THE DIFFERENCE IS STRESS-INDUCED. The baseline equality is the control that makes the stress-induced difference readable, and it also forbids a claim that WWOX loss raises ROS in unstressed primary fibroblasts.
entries.snippet: No differences in the amounts of ROS generation were observed between the freshly isolated Wwox+/+ and Wwox−/− MEFs

entries.proposition: The stress applied is removal of serum from the culture medium (serum-free RPMI-1640), not glucose or calorie restriction; the paper does not describe medium glucose or any glucose manipulation.
